script.title: Capital vs Revenue Expenditure
script.caption_hook: Machine and its repair: why are they treated so differently?

lines.say: Ma'am, I paid for a machine and its repair. Why different treatment?
Good question! Ask one thing first: does the benefit last many years, or just this year?

board.title: Capital vs Revenue
board.sub: Years of benefit, or this year?

lines.say: So a machine is for years, but repairs are just for now?
Exactly. Machine is capital, shown in the Balance Sheet. Repairs are revenue, charged to Profit and Loss Account.
What if I also pay freight and installation for the machine?
Those are capital too. Machine ₹50,000, freight ₹2,000, installation ₹3,000. Asset cost becomes ₹55,000.
And an ordinary repair of ₹1,000 later?
That only keeps it running, so it's revenue. Charge ₹1,000 to Profit and Loss Account.
Is a repair always revenue, then?
No. Repairs to make a second-hand machine usable at purchase are capital. Size of the amount never decides.
Oh! Purpose decides, not the amount.
Remember, capital means cement the asset. Cemented in is capital; only keeps it running is revenue.
